summary: The note announces the Local Business Fair, running September 8th to 10th, 2023 at the community center on Elm Street, themed "Supporting Our Home-Grown Entrepreneurs." It describes over 200 local businesses, workshops, seminars, networking, and family activities, with quotes from local entrepreneurs and officials. The central message is that supporting local business should be a continuous commitment that strengthens the local economy and community.
one_line: The Local Business Fair, September 8-10, 2023, showcases over 200 local businesses and urges lasting community support for home-grown entrepreneurs.
key_facts: The Local Business Fair runs from September 8th to 10th, 2023 at the community center on Elm Street.
The fair's theme this year is "Supporting Our Home-Grown Entrepreneurs."
The fair is expected to feature over 200 local businesses, from handcrafted jewelry to bespoke software solutions.
Attendees can enjoy food tastings of locally sourced products, live craftsmanship demonstrations, and interactive workshops led by business leaders.
Melissa Thompson, a local artisan and repeat fair participant, calls the fair a springboard for small businesses to gain exposure and connect with new customers.
James Peterson, president of the local Chamber of Commerce, says every dollar spent at the fair will weave its way back through multiple layers of the local economy.
Cindy Hughes launched her stationery business at last year's fair and said the feedback was like wind in her sails.
Thomas Anderson, a photographer and storyteller, will create a multimedia exhibit capturing entrepreneurs' personal journeys.
City Council member Linda Martinez urges residents to integrate supporting local businesses into daily life rather than treating it as a one-off.
The "Kids' Entrepreneurial Corner" is a new addition this year, featuring face painting and a small-scale business pitch competition for children.
Seminars and panels cover social media marketing, financial planning for small businesses, and creating a sustainable business model.
Erica Johnson, a local marketing consultant, is among the seasoned professionals who crafted the educational sessions.
Startup founders can connect with investors, and established businesses can share resources and mentorship with newer ones.
